S1Q05.answerFind: The ColumnTransformer fits exclusively on the training split—handling missing numeric values with an imputer and encoding categoricals with unknown category handling—so no validation statistics ever bleed into training.
S1Q05.answerReplace: The ColumnTransformer is fit once on the full dataset before the split—handling missing numeric values with an imputer and encoding categoricals with unknown category handling—so every statistic is computed on all available rows.

S1Q06F.answerFind: simple append-only logs fail because past feature values shift, so I'd introduce an updated-at timestamp or event versioning, and run scheduled backfill pipelines to recompute affected snapshots cleanly
S1Q06F.answerReplace: simple append-only logs remain sufficient because corrections never change past feature values, so I'd add no versioning and never recompute any snapshot

S1Q07F.fullPhrase: Pin the model artifact and feature snapshot together

S1Q08F.answerFind: Training on past data where campaigns were active creates a feedback loop that distorts true customer behavior. If an incentive successfully kept a high-risk customer from churning, the model learns that this profile stays, even though they would have left without the intervention. That means future predictions end up measuring response to marketing rather than baseline churn risk.
S1Q08F.answerReplace: Training on customers affected by previous campaigns does not introduce bias, because a campaign only changes behavior in ways the model can already see. Incentives simply reveal true customer preferences, so the observed labels are a clean measure of baseline churn risk. Repeated retraining on that data therefore keeps the model accurate.

S2Q04F.answerFind: Raw scores from keyword and vector searches live on completely different scales, so adding them directly lets whichever model outputs larger numbers dominate the results.
S2Q04F.answerReplace: Raw scores from keyword and vector searches already share one normalized scale, so adding them directly is a perfectly good way to merge the results.

S2Q07F.answerFind: Authorization must be checked twice: at the initial retrieval filter and right before context injection. If permissions change mid-query, relying only on a pre-flight check can leak data if chunks are already in flight. I enforce late-binding authorization by validating document ACLs against retrieved chunk metadata immediately before sending the payload to the LLM.
S2Q07F.answerReplace: Authorization needs to be checked only once, at query start. If permissions change mid-query, the result is still valid because the user was entitled when the query began. I enforce early-binding authorization by validating the user's ACLs at query start and never re-checking the retrieved chunks.

S2Q09F.answerFind: region-specific Azure OpenAI deployments to guarantee inference and embeddings stay fully within that geography
S2Q09F.answerReplace: global Azure OpenAI deployments, which guarantee inference and embeddings stay within that geography
